Health and safety 
We train employees at our facilities regularly on general safety guidelines and safe work procedures and undertake 
regular safety drills. The monthly injury rate in our network stood at 0.20 per thousand employees (on-roll as 
well as off-roll) as of December 31, 2021. In addition, we conduct regular health camps for our workforce and 
have ambulances available at our key centers. 
 
Disaster recovery and business continuity 
 
We are committed to maintaining the continuity of our business, including all activities, systems, facilities and 
processes which are necessary to provide services to our clients and customers. Accordingly, we have set up a 
disaster recovery and business continuity plan which sets out the details of the individuals responsible for disaster 
assessment and the procedures to be followed in the event of a disaster. In the event of a disaster that interferes 
with our ability to conduct our business, the plan will be implemented by the individuals responsible for 
coordinating the business recovery of their respective areas or departments to minimize the impact on the quality 
of our services. The disaster assessment team is responsible for assessing the extent of the damage and loss, 
identifying, characterizing and quantifying the damages, defining and prioritizing the actions and resources to 
reduce immediate risks, identifying the priority of actions required and estimating the additional support required 
for recovery. In addition, we have established various controls and safety devices to minimize the potential 
impacts of a fire, an electricity or IT outage, disasters related to our data and applications and breakdowns of our 
sorters, and to preserve the health and safety of our workforce, including smoke detection systems, emergency 
evacuation drills with fire brigades in larger facilities, mandatory online trainings on fire and safety on a quarterly 
basis, regular audits and checks of wiring and connections and database backups, per the established policies.  
 
OUR TEAM  
As of December 31, 2021, excluding Spoton, we had 15,392 permanent employees worldwide and engaged 
manpower agencies to provide us with a temporary workforce, which included 36,956 contracted workers 
(excluding daily wage manpower, security guards and Spoton), as of December 31, 2021. In addition, excluding 
Spoton, we had 33,836 last mile delivery agents in the month of December 2021. Spoton had 1,831 permanent 
employees and 261 contract workers as of December 31, 2021. Our network partners hire their own employees 
according to their operational needs. None of our employees are represented by a labour union. We maintain a 
good working relationship with our employees, and we have not experienced any work stoppages since our 
incorporation.

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY 
We rely on a combination of trademarks, copyrights and patents in India and other jurisdictions in which we 
operate, as well as confidentiality procedures and contractual provisions to protect our intellectual property. 
 
We have filed the following patents in India and/or the U.S., which are currently pending:

request.system:
You extract checkable facts from one page of a document.

You see the rendered page image and the machine-extracted text layer. The text layer is often
corrupted: table rows shift, columns interleave, currency glyphs vanish or turn into stray letters,
footnote markers glue onto numbers. Trust the IMAGE for what a number is and where it sits in a
table; use the TEXT LAYER only to copy quotes.

What counts as a fact: a specific claim about a named entity with a numeric value (or a definite
categorical statement such as a rating, a rank or a classification) that another document could
agree or disagree with. Include prose numbers, headline table cells (totals, latest period, named
indicators) and KPIs on slides. Exclude page numbers, section numbers, table-of-contents lines,
chart axis ticks, dates on their own, boilerplate and values that are only labels. In dense tables
prefer the latest period and totals. Return at most 25 facts, most important first.

Fields:
- entity: who or what the fact is about. attribute: the measured quantity as a short noun phrase
  with no period or unit in it. Reuse names from the existing vocabulary when they mean the same.
- value: exactly as printed, including brackets or "(-)". unit: as printed. scale: the scale word
  from the row, column or table header ("million", "crore", "lakh", "billion"), never guessed.
- period: as printed. period_start/period_end: your ISO-date reading using the document's fiscal
  year convention. Quarters, halves and cumulative spans are their own periods; "as on" dates are
  points in time (start = end).
- estimate_type: from the document's own labels (provisional, advance estimate, revised, budget,
  projection, target, scenario). Use third_party and fill attributed_to when the document reports
  another organisation's figure.
- measurement_basis: any qualifier that changes comparability ("consolidated", "standalone",
  "BoP basis", "as % of GDP", "excluding X", "pro forma", "authorities' definition").
- quote: a contiguous verbatim substring of the TEXT LAYER that contains the value (≤300 chars,
  may include the row label). If the value is visible in the image but absent or garbled in the
  text layer, set quote_source to "image" and write the label and value as you read them.
  Never paraphrase a quote.
- confidence: how sure you are the value, unit, period and entity are all right.

Also report page_kind and a short list of problems you noticed while reading the page.
